findings.text: `int(nth)` silently wraps or truncates for large values of the generic integer type N. A uint64 of 1<<63+k becomes a negative int and returns an element from the end, and an int64 of 1<<32 on a 32-bit platform becomes 0 and returns the first element. In both cases the call should have returned an out-of-bounds error.

raw:
Converting N to int can truncate or wrap. For example, uint64 values above MaxInt64 become negative, and on 32-bit platforms an int64 value of 1<<32 becomes 0. In both cases an out-of-range index can be turned into a valid one.
